+\section{Fixed-base linear depth for Pisot numeration}
+\label{sec:pisot-linear-depth}
+
+We now pass from Parry families to a fixed standard numeration system.  A
+Pisot numeration system is a sequence $U=(u_j)_{j\ge0}$ of positive integers
+which satisfies the integral recurrence whose characteristic polynomial is
+the minimal polynomial of a Pisot number; the initial values need not be the
+standard ones.  We assume throughout this section that $U$ is strictly
+increasing and $u_0=1$.  Let
+\[
+D_U=\{0,\ldots,d_U\}
+\]
+be its canonical greedy digit set.  The canonical greedy $U$-normal words of
+length $m$ are
+\begin{equation}
+X_{U,m}=\left\{x\in D_U^m:
+ \sum_{j=0}^k x_ju_j<u_{k+1}\quad(0\le k<m)\right\}.
+\label{eq:pisot-canonical-words}
+\end{equation}
+Thus
+\[
+\Val_{U,m}(x)=\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}x_ju_j
+\]
+maps $X_{U,m}$ bijectively onto $\{0,\ldots,u_m-1\}$.  Define
+\begin{equation}
+\Fold_{U,m}(w)=
+(\Val_{U,m}|_{X_{U,m}})^{-1}
+       (\Val_{U,m}(w)\bmod u_m)
+\label{eq:pisot-canonical-fold}
+\end{equation}
+and let $\Phi_{U,m}$ be the corresponding sliding code on
+$D_U^{\mathbb Z}$.  We use the convention in
+\eqref{eq:simple-parry-causal-length} for $\ell_{\rm cau}(U,m)$.
+
+Put $\Delta_U=[-d_U,d_U]\cap\mathbb Z$ and, for $L\ge1$, set
+\begin{equation}
+\mathcal N_{U,m,L}=\left\{e\in\Delta_U^{m+L-1}:
+ e_0\ne0,\quad
+ \sum_{j=0}^{m-1}u_je_{t+j}\equiv0\pmod {u_m}
+ \ (0\le t<L)\right\}.
+\label{eq:pisot-bad-sliding-set}
+\end{equation}
+Every row in this system has a uniquely defined carry $k_t\in\mathbb Z$:
+\begin{equation}
+\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}u_je_{t+j}=k_tu_m.
+\label{eq:pisot-window-carry}
+\end{equation}
+Equivalently,
+\begin{equation}
+[e_t,e_{t+1},\ldots,e_{t+m-1},-k_t]_U=0,
+\label{eq:pisot-zero-word-bridge}
+\end{equation}
+where the last coordinate has weight $u_m$.  This is the promised bridge to
+the standard language of bounded zero representations; it is not an
+identification with numerical $\beta$-normalization.
+
+\begin{lemma}[Exact collision quotient for $U$]
+\label{lem:pisot-exact-collision-quotient}
+For every $m\ge2$,
+\begin{equation}
+\ell_{\rm cau}(U,m)
+=\min\{L\ge1:\mathcal N_{U,m,L}=\varnothing\}.
+\label{eq:pisot-exact-depth}
+\end{equation}
+Let $\Gamma_{U,m}$ have vertex set $\Delta_U^{m-1}$ and an edge
+$(v_0,\ldots,v_{m-2})\to(v_1,\ldots,v_{m-2},a)$ exactly when
+\[
+\sum_{j=0}^{m-2}u_jv_j+u_{m-1}a\equiv0\pmod {u_m}.
+\]
+If $B_{U,m}$ is the set of vertices with first coordinate nonzero, then
+\begin{equation}
+\ell_{\rm cau}(U,m)=1+sup\{\text{edge length of a path from }B_{U,m}\}.
+\label{eq:pisot-longest-path}
+\end{equation}
+Moreover, $\Phi_{U,m}$ is injective if and only if no directed cycle of
+$\Gamma_{U,m}$ is reachable from $B_{U,m}$.
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:simple-parry-causal-collision} uses only the
+bijection between normal words and the residue interval, together with the
+fact that every $e\in\Delta_U$ is the difference of its positive and
+negative parts in $D_U$.  Those two facts hold here, so the same quotient of
+the classical pair graph gives \eqref{eq:pisot-exact-depth} and
+\eqref{eq:pisot-longest-path}.  A nonzero bi-infinite path is again realized
+by two raw points, and a reachable cycle can be repeated periodically.
+
+It remains only to note why injectivity rules out the zero loop as a
+reachable cycle.  If $d_U\ge u_m$, the constant nonzero difference sequence
+$e_t=u_m$ belongs to $\Delta_U^{\mathbb Z}$ and every window sum is divisible
+by $u_m$; hence $\Phi_{U,m}$ is noninjective and the difference graph has a
+nonzero loop.  In the only remaining case, $d_U<u_m$.  If a vertex has an
+edge to the zero vertex, its overlap coordinates vanish and its first
+coordinate $a$ satisfies $a\equiv0\pmod {u_m}$.  The bound $|a|\le d_U<u_m$
+then gives $a=0$, so the zero vertex is its own unique predecessor.  This
+proves the last assertion without imposing a restriction on the allowed
+nonstandard initial values.
+\end{proof}
+
+We next make the contraction constant explicit.  Let
+$\beta=\beta_0,\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_{s-1}$ be the roots of the minimal
+polynomial, with $\beta>1$ and $|\beta_i|<1$ for $i\ge1$.  The recurrence and
+the initial values effectively give algebraic numbers $c_i$ such that
+\begin{equation}
+u_n=\sum_{i=0}^{s-1}c_i\beta_i^n,
+\qquad c_0>0.
+\label{eq:pisot-binet}
+\end{equation}
+Effective root isolation gives positive algebraic bounds $b_U,A_U$ with
+\begin{equation}
+b_U\beta^n\le u_n\le A_U\beta^n\qquad(n\ge0).
+\label{eq:pisot-effective-growth}
+\end{equation}
+Indeed, isolate a point after which the total conjugate contribution in
+\eqref{eq:pisot-binet} is at most $c_0\beta^n/2$, and inspect the remaining
+finite prefix.
+
+Set
+\begin{equation}
+\widehat K_U=
+\left\lceil\frac{d_UA_U}{b_U(\beta-1)}\right\rceil.
+\label{eq:pisot-analytic-carry-bound}
+\end{equation}
+The bounded-zero normalization automaton may now be intersected with the
+finite terminal alphabet $[-\widehat K_U,\widehat K_U]$.  Let
+$\mathcal K_U$ be the set of terminal carries $k$ for which that automaton
+accepts a word of the form in \eqref{eq:pisot-zero-word-bridge}, and put
+$K_U=\max_{k\in\mathcal K_U}|k|$.  Finite automaton reachability computes
+this set.  Equation \eqref{eq:pisot-effective-growth} shows directly that
+every carry in \eqref{eq:pisot-window-carry} belongs to it, since
+\[
+|k_t|\le d_U\frac{\sum_{j<m}u_j}{u_m}
+<\frac{d_UA_U}{b_U(\beta-1)}.
+\]
+
+For nonintegral $\beta$, define the effective positive separation
+\begin{equation}
+\delta_U=\min\left\{|a+k-\beta l|:
+ a\in\Delta_U,\ k,l\in\mathcal K_U,\ a+k-\beta l\ne0\right\}
+\label{eq:pisot-effective-separation}
+\end{equation}
+and
+\begin{equation}
+M_U=\frac1{c_0}\sum_{i=1}^{s-1}|c_i|
+ \left(\frac{d_U}{1-|\beta_i|}+K_U\right),
+\qquad
+B_U=d_U+(1+\beta)M_U.
+\label{eq:pisot-conjugate-bound}
+\end{equation}
+The minimum in \eqref{eq:pisot-effective-separation} is positive: if
+$l\ne0$, irrationality of $\beta$ prevents equality with the integer
+$a+k$, while for $l=0$ every nonzero value has modulus at least one.  All
+comparisons are comparisons of algebraic numbers and are effective.
+Finally let
+\begin{equation}
+m_U=\min\{m\ge2:\beta^m\delta_U>B_U\}.
+\label{eq:pisot-contraction-threshold}
+\end{equation}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Adjacent-window Pisot contraction]
+\label{lem:pisot-adjacent-window-contraction}
+Suppose that $\beta$ is nonintegral, $m\ge m_U$, and two consecutive rows
+of \eqref{eq:pisot-window-carry} hold.  Then
+\begin{equation}
+k_{t+1}=0,\qquad e_{t+m}=-k_t.
+\label{eq:pisot-carry-collapse}
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+For each embedding define
+\[
+A_{t,i}=\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}e_{t+j}\beta_i^j-k_t\beta_i^m.
+\]
+Substitution of \eqref{eq:pisot-binet} into
+\eqref{eq:pisot-window-carry} gives
+$\sum_i c_iA_{t,i}=0$.  For $i\ge1$,
+\[
+|A_{t,i}|\le \frac{d_U}{1-|\beta_i|}+K_U,
+\]
+and therefore $|A_{t,0}|\le M_U$.  Direct subtraction of two adjacent
+dominant-embedding sums yields
+\begin{equation}
+\beta^m(e_{t+m}+k_t-\beta k_{t+1})
+=\beta A_{t+1,0}-A_{t,0}+e_t.
+\label{eq:pisot-adjacent-binet-identity}
+\end{equation}
+The right side has modulus at most $B_U$.  By
+\eqref{eq:pisot-effective-separation} and
+\eqref{eq:pisot-contraction-threshold}, the parenthesis on the left must
+vanish.  Since $e_{t+m}+k_t$ and $k_{t+1}$ are integers and $\beta$ is
+irrational, this is possible only in \eqref{eq:pisot-carry-collapse}.
+\end{proof}
+
+For $2\le m<m_U$, let $p_U(m)$ be the maximum edge length of a path from
+$B_{U,m}$ when no directed cycle is reachable from $B_{U,m}$, and put
+$p_U(m)=0$ otherwise.  This finite list is computed by exact acyclic
+longest-path searches.  Define
+\begin{equation}
+C_U=\max\left(2,
+ \max_{2\le m<m_U}\left\lceil\frac{1+p_U(m)}m\right\rceil\right).
+\label{eq:effective-linear-constant}
+\end{equation}
+This is a finite, effective recipe from the recurrence, the canonical digit
+set, and the bounded-zero normalization automaton.  The large-aperture part
+of the recipe is the Pisot contraction estimate, not a count of the
+$(2d_U+1)^{m-1}$ difference vertices.
+
+\begin{theorem}[Fixed-base linear causal depth and sharpness for Pisot numeration]
+\label{thm:pisot-linear-depth-sharpness}
+Let $U=(u_j)_{j\ge0}$ be a strictly increasing Pisot numeration system,
+with nonstandard initial values allowed, $u_0=1$, canonical greedy digit set
+$D_U=\{0,\ldots,d_U\}$, and canonical normal words
+\eqref{eq:pisot-canonical-words}.  Assume that $U$ preserves zeros, or,
+equivalently, that its leading Pisot root satisfies Condition~F.  Then the
+constant $C_U<\infty$ in \eqref{eq:effective-linear-constant} is effectively
+computable from the recurrence, the canonical digit set, and the
+bounded-zero normalization automaton, and, for every $m\ge2$,
+\refstepcounter{equation}
+\begin{equation}
+\Phi_{U,m}\text{ injective}
+\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
+\ell_{\rm cau}(U,m)\le C_Um.
+\tag{A1}\label{eq:pisot-linear-A1}
+\end{equation}
+Equivalently, if no first-coordinate-nonzero state of $\Gamma_{U,m}$ can
+reach a directed cycle, every directed path from that initial state set has
+length at most $C_Um-1$.
+
+Let $\theta$ be the real root of
+\[
+x^3-2x^2+x-1
+\]
+and let $U_\theta=(Q_j(\theta))_{j\ge0}$ be given by
+\begin{equation}
+Q_0(\theta)=1,\quad Q_1(\theta)=2,\quad Q_2(\theta)=4,
+\quad Q_{j+3}(\theta)=2Q_{j+2}(\theta)-Q_{j+1}(\theta)+Q_j(\theta).
+\label{eq:theta-count-recurrence}
+\end{equation}
+For every $m\ge4$,
+\refstepcounter{equation}
+\begin{equation}
+\Phi_{\theta,m}\text{ is injective},\qquad
+\ell_{\rm cau}(\theta,m)=2\left\lfloor\frac m2\right\rfloor-1.
+\tag{A2}\label{eq:pisot-linear-A2}
+\end{equation}
+More precisely, if
+$\lambda_m=2\lfloor m/2\rfloor-1$, then
+\refstepcounter{equation}
+\begin{equation}
+\mathcal N_{\theta,m,\lambda_m-1}=\{E_m,-E_m\}\ne\varnothing,
+\qquad
+\mathcal N_{\theta,m,\lambda_m}=\varnothing,
+\tag{A3}\label{eq:pisot-linear-A3}
+\end{equation}
+where, writing concatenation by juxtaposition and changing every sign by a
+prefixed minus,
+\begin{equation}
+\begin{gathered}
+E_4=(1,-1,-1,-1,1),\\
+E_m=(1,0,-E_{m-2},0,0)\quad(m\ge6\text{ even}),\\
+E_m=(E_{m-1},0)\quad(m\ge5\text{ odd}).
+\end{gathered}
+\label{eq:theta-terminal-word}
+\end{equation}
+Consequently
+\[
+\lim_{m\to\infty}\frac{\ell_{\rm cau}(\theta,m)}m=1,
+\]
+so the fixed-system linear upper bound cannot be improved to $o(m)$ in
+growth order.
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+We first prove \eqref{eq:pisot-linear-A1}.  The degree-one case is
+$u_j=b^j$, $D_U=\{0,\ldots,b-1\}$; its fold is the identity and
+$\ell_{\rm cau}(U,m)=1$.  Suppose that $\beta$ is nonintegral and
+$m\ge m_U$.  If a vector in $\mathcal N_{U,m,L}$ has $L\ge2$, apply
+Lemma~\ref{lem:pisot-adjacent-window-contraction} for
+$0\le t\le L-2$.  It gives
+\[
+k_1=\cdots=k_{L-1}=0,\qquad
+e_m=-k_0,\qquad e_{m+1}=\cdots=e_{m+L-2}=0.
+\]
+If $L=m+1$, the terminal difference vertex is therefore zero.  It cannot
+be reached from $B_{U,m}$ when no directed cycle is reachable, because the
+zero vertex has a loop.  Hence every such path has at most $m$ edges and
+$\ell_{\rm cau}(U,m)\le m+1\le2m$.  The finitely many smaller apertures are
+covered by the definition of $C_U$.  Lemma
+\ref{lem:pisot-exact-collision-quotient} gives both formulations of
+\eqref{eq:pisot-linear-A1}.
+
+We turn to $\theta$.  The polynomial is negative at $7/4$, positive at
+$351/200$, and has only one real zero; the product of the two nonreal roots
+has modulus $1/\theta$.  Thus $\theta$ is Pisot.  Its defining equation
+gives
+\[
+1=\theta^{-1}+\theta^{-2}+\theta^{-4},
+\]
+and every proper suffix of $1101\,0^\infty$ is lexicographically smaller.
+Parry's criterion therefore gives $d_\theta(1)=1101\,0^\infty$.  The
+canonical language counts are exactly \eqref{eq:theta-count-recurrence}.
+In particular, the digit and difference alphabets are $\{0,1\}$ and
+$\{-1,0,1\}$.  The recurrence also implies the positive recurrence
+$Q_{n+4}=Q_{n+3}+Q_{n+2}+Q_n$.  Thus
+$2Q_{n+1}-3Q_n>0$ follows from its four positive initial values.  Starting
+with $Q_0<2Q_1$ and using
+$\sum_{j<m+1}Q_j<3Q_m<2Q_{m+1}$ then gives
+\begin{equation}
+\sum_{j<m}Q_j(\theta)<2Q_m(\theta),
+\label{eq:theta-carry-one}
+\end{equation}
+so every window carry belongs to $\{-1,0,1\}$.
+
+For completeness, we verify the contraction threshold rather than invoking
+an unspecified asymptotic.  If $\rho,\overline\rho$ are the nonreal roots,
+write
+\[
+Q_n=c_\theta\theta^n+c_\rho\rho^n+overline{c_\rho}\,\overline\rho^n.
+\]
+The rational isolating interval above and the residue formula for the
+generating function
+\[
+\sum_{n\ge0}Q_nz^n=\frac{1+z^2}{1-2z+z^2-z^3}
+\]
+give
+\[
+1.26<c_\theta<1.27,\qquad |c_\rho|<0.19,\qquad |\rho|<0.756.
+\]
+Hence the dominant-embedding error in the proof of Lemma
+\ref{lem:pisot-adjacent-window-contraction} is less than $1.54$.  Here
+$\delta_\theta=2-\theta>0.245$, and
+\[
+\theta^6\delta_\theta>7.03
+>1+(1+\theta)1.54.
+\]
+It follows that \eqref{eq:pisot-carry-collapse} holds for every $m\ge6$.
+The apertures $m=4,5$ will be included in the exact terminal check below.
+
+It remains to classify the longest paths.  Fix $m\ge6$ and a vector with
+at least two collision rows.  After the carry collapse, all its coordinates
+beyond $m$ vanish except possibly $e_m=-k_0$.  Define the full suffix sums
+\[
+R_t=\sum_{j\ge0}Q_j(\theta)e_{t+j}.
+\]
+Every collision row with $t\ge1$ is now $R_t=0$, and the first row together
+with $e_m=-k_0$ gives $R_0=0$.  The recurrence implies the exact identity
+\begin{equation}
+R_t=e_t+e_{t+2}+2R_{t+1}-R_{t+2}+R_{t+3}.
+\label{eq:theta-suffix-renormalization}
+\end{equation}
+Thus four consecutive zero suffix sums force $e_t=-e_{t+2}$.
+
+Let first $m$ be even and take $L=m-2=\lambda_m-1$.  We have
+$R_t=0$ for $0\le t\le m-3$.  The terminal equation is
+\[
+e_{m-3}+2e_{m-2}+4e_{m-1}+7e_m=0.
+\]
+In $\{-1,0,1\}^4$ its complete solution set is
+\begin{equation}
+(0,0,0,0),\qquad \pm(1,1,1,-1).
+\label{eq:theta-four-tail-table}
+\end{equation}
+The zero tail propagates backwards to the zero word.  From a nonzero tail,
+the equations $R_{m-4}=R_{m-5}=0$ give respectively
+$e_{m-4}=-e_{m-3}$ and $e_{m-5}=0$; then
+\eqref{eq:theta-suffix-renormalization} propagates the alternating pair
+uniquely to the left.  This is precisely the recursion
+\eqref{eq:theta-terminal-word}, and both signs occur.  Hence the first set
+in \eqref{eq:pisot-linear-A3} is $\{\pm E_m\}$.  With one more row, the
+terminal equation is
+\[
+e_{m-2}+2e_{m-1}+4e_m=0,
+\]
+whose only solution in $\{-1,0,1\}^3$ is zero.  Backward propagation then
+contradicts $e_0\ne0$.  Thus $\mathcal N_{\theta,m,\lambda_m}$ is empty.
+
+Now let $m$ be odd and take $L=m-3=\lambda_m-1$.  The terminal five-digit
+equation has, up to sign, exactly the following solutions:
+\begin{equation}
+(0,0,0,0,0),\quad
+(1,1,1,-1,0),\quad
+(1,0,1,1,-1),\quad
+(1,-1,-1,-1,1).
+\label{eq:theta-five-tail-table}
+\end{equation}
+Successive solution of $R_{m-5}=0$ gives respectively
+$0,-1,0,0$ for the preceding digit.  Since $m-5$ is even,
+\eqref{eq:theta-suffix-renormalization} propagates this digit to $e_0$ up
+to sign.  The zero tail and the last two nonzero tails therefore give
+$e_0=0$; only $\pm(1,1,1,-1,0)$ survive.  They give exactly the even
+terminal word for aperture $m-1$ followed by zero, namely $\pm E_m$.
+With one more row the terminal four-digit alternatives are
+\eqref{eq:theta-four-tail-table}; now $m-5$ has even parity and its forced
+zero propagates to $e_0$.  Hence the next obstruction set is empty.
+
+For $m=4,5$, successive exact division in the two or three window
+congruences gives
+\[
+\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
+m&Q_m&\mathcal N_{\theta,m,\lambda_m-1}
+&\mathcal N_{\theta,m,\lambda_m}\\ \hline
+4&12&\{\pm(1,-1,-1,-1,1)\}&\varnothing\\
+5&21&\{\pm(1,-1,-1,-1,1,0)\}&\varnothing.
+\end{array}
+\]
+This is an exhaustive integer calculation: in each row the quotient is in
+$\{-1,0,1\}$ by \eqref{eq:theta-carry-one}, and the last digit determines
+the preceding bounded digit successively.  Thus \eqref{eq:pisot-linear-A3}
+holds for every $m\ge4$.  Lemma
+\ref{lem:pisot-exact-collision-quotient} now gives
+\eqref{eq:pisot-linear-A2}, including injectivity, and the limiting statement
+is immediate.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{corollary}[Bounded-zero strip synchronization]
+\label{cor:pisot-zero-strip-synchronization}
+For a fixed zero-preserving Pisot numeration $U$, consider bounded zero words
+of length $m+1$ of the form
+\[
+[e_t,\ldots,e_{t+m-1},-k_t]_U=0
+\]
+which overlap one digit at a time.  Either
+the resulting strip pumps to a periodic bounded zero representation, or it
+synchronizes in at most $(C_U+1)m$ rows.  This order is $\Theta(m)$ for
+$U_\theta$.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The overlapping rows are exactly paths in $\Gamma_{U,m}$ by
+\eqref{eq:pisot-zero-word-bridge}.  Unless the strip is zero, at most $m-1$
+initial rows pass before a nonzero coordinate occupies the first position.
+A pumpable strip is then a reachable directed cycle; otherwise
+\eqref{eq:pisot-linear-A1} gives the remaining bound.  The words $E_m$ in
+\eqref{eq:pisot-linear-A3} give the matching lower order for $U_\theta$.
+\end{proof}

+The central conclusion is a fixed-system complexity theorem on a standard
+numeration class.  For every strictly increasing zero-preserving Pisot
+numeration $U$, including systems with nonstandard initial values, Theorem

+def theta_terminal_vector(m: int) -> tuple[int, ...]:
+    """Return the positive-first extremal word E_m for the fixed cubic base."""
+    if m < 4:
+        raise ValueError("the fixed-theta theorem begins at aperture m=4")
+    even_aperture = m if m % 2 == 0 else m - 1
+    core = (1, -1, -1, -1, 1)
+    for aperture in range(6, even_aperture + 1, 2):
+        core = (1, 0) + tuple(-entry for entry in core)
+        if len(core) != aperture + 1:
+            raise AssertionError("the two-step terminal recursion lost its aperture")
+    vector = core + (0,) * (even_aperture - 4)
+    if m % 2:
+        vector += (0,)
+    return vector

 \begin{abstract}
-We study the symbolic dynamics of a cyclic recoding of greedy
-$\beta$-languages.  The canonical Parry--Bertrand rank of a legal length-$m$
-word is extended to the full digit cube, reduced modulo the number
-$Q_m(\beta)$ of legal words, and overlapped along consecutive windows.  This
-is a congruence of integer language ranks, not numerical

+We study the symbolic dynamics of cyclic recodings of greedy Pisot
+numeration systems.  The canonical rank of a legal length-$m$ word is
+extended to the full digit cube, reduced modulo the number $u_m$ of legal
+words, and overlapped along consecutive windows.  This is a congruence of
+integer language ranks, not numerical $\beta$-normalization in
+$\mathbb Z[\beta]$.
+
+Our first main result is uniform over standard Pisot numeration systems.  If
+a fixed strictly increasing system $U=(u_j)$ preserves zeros, equivalently
+its leading root satisfies Condition~F, there is an effectively computable
+constant $C_U$ such that every injective aperture-$m$ recoding satisfies
 \[
+\ell_{\rm cau}(U,m)\le C_Um.
+\]
+The constant is computed from the recurrence, canonical digit set, and
+bounded-zero normalization automaton.  The proof uses the contracting Pisot
+conjugates to collapse adjacent window carries; it is not a count of the
+exponentially many difference states.  The order is sharp.  For the fixed
+binary cubic system whose leading root $\theta$ satisfies
+$\theta^3-2\theta^2+\theta-1=0$, every $m\ge4$ is injective and
+\[
+\ell_{\rm cau}(\theta,m)=2\lfloor m/2\rfloor-1.
+\]

 \medskip
+\noindent\textbf{Fixed-base Pisot linear depth.}
+Let $U=(u_j)$ be a strictly increasing Pisot numeration system with
+canonical digit set $D_U=\{0,\ldots,d_U\}$; nonstandard initial values are
+allowed.  Assume that $U$ preserves zeros, equivalently that its leading
+Pisot root satisfies Condition~F
+\cite{FrougnySolomyak1992,CartonSudberyYassawi2026}.  Theorem
+\ref{thm:pisot-linear-depth-sharpness} proves that there is an effectively
+computable $C_U<\infty$ such that
+\[
+\Phi_{U,m}\text{ injective}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
+\ell_{\rm cau}(U,m)\le C_Um\qquad(m\ge2).
+\]
+The constant is obtained from the recurrence, the canonical digit set, and
+the bounded-zero normalization automaton.  Each collision window becomes a
+standard bounded zero representation
+\[
+[e_t,\ldots,e_{t+m-1},-k_t]_U=0.
+\]
+A Binet estimate in the contracting conjugate directions then collapses two
+adjacent carries beyond an effective aperture.  Hence all but one appended
+difference vanish; a path surviving more than linearly many rows would
+reach the zero loop and violate injectivity.  Only finitely many smaller
+apertures require exact graph searches.  Thus the bound uses Pisot
+contraction and normalization data rather than the exponential vertex count
+$(2d_U+1)^{m-1}$.

+\section{Fixed-base linear depth for Pisot numeration}
+\label{sec:pisot-linear-depth}
+
+We now pass from Parry families to a fixed standard numeration system.  A
+Pisot numeration system is a sequence $U=(u_j)_{j\ge0}$ of positive integers
+which satisfies the integral recurrence whose characteristic polynomial is
+the minimal polynomial of a Pisot number; the initial values need not be the
+standard ones.  We assume throughout this section that $U$ is strictly
+increasing and $u_0=1$.  Let
+\[
+D_U=\{0,\ldots,d_U\}
+\]
+be its canonical greedy digit set.  The canonical greedy $U$-normal words of
+length $m$ are
+\begin{equation}
+X_{U,m}=\left\{x\in D_U^m:
+ \sum_{j=0}^k x_ju_j<u_{k+1}\quad(0\le k<m)\right\}.
+\label{eq:pisot-canonical-words}
+\end{equation}
+Thus
+\[
+\Val_{U,m}(x)=\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}x_ju_j
+\]
+maps $X_{U,m}$ bijectively onto $\{0,\ldots,u_m-1\}$.  Define
+\begin{equation}
+\Fold_{U,m}(w)=
+(\Val_{U,m}|_{X_{U,m}})^{-1}
+       (\Val_{U,m}(w)\bmod u_m)
+\label{eq:pisot-canonical-fold}
+\end{equation}
+and let $\Phi_{U,m}$ be the corresponding sliding code on
+$D_U^{\mathbb Z}$.  We use the convention in
+\eqref{eq:simple-parry-causal-length} for $\ell_{\rm cau}(U,m)$.
+
+Put $\Delta_U=[-d_U,d_U]\cap\mathbb Z$ and, for $L\ge1$, set
+\begin{equation}
+\mathcal N_{U,m,L}=\left\{e\in\Delta_U^{m+L-1}:
+ e_0\ne0,\quad
+ \sum_{j=0}^{m-1}u_je_{t+j}\equiv0\pmod {u_m}
+ \ (0\le t<L)\right\}.
+\label{eq:pisot-bad-sliding-set}
+\end{equation}
+Every row in this system has a uniquely defined carry $k_t\in\mathbb Z$:
+\begin{equation}
+\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}u_je_{t+j}=k_tu_m.
+\label{eq:pisot-window-carry}
+\end{equation}
+Equivalently,
+\begin{equation}
+[e_t,e_{t+1},\ldots,e_{t+m-1},-k_t]_U=0,
+\label{eq:pisot-zero-word-bridge}
+\end{equation}
+where the last coordinate has weight $u_m$.  This is the promised bridge to
+the standard language of bounded zero representations; it is not an
+identification with numerical $\beta$-normalization.
+
+\begin{lemma}[Exact collision quotient for $U$]
+\label{lem:pisot-exact-collision-quotient}
+For every $m\ge2$,
+\begin{equation}
+\ell_{\rm cau}(U,m)
+=\min\{L\ge1:\mathcal N_{U,m,L}=\varnothing\}.
+\label{eq:pisot-exact-depth}
+\end{equation}
+Let $\Gamma_{U,m}$ have vertex set $\Delta_U^{m-1}$ and an edge
+$(v_0,\ldots,v_{m-2})\to(v_1,\ldots,v_{m-2},a)$ exactly when
+\[
+\sum_{j=0}^{m-2}u_jv_j+u_{m-1}a\equiv0\pmod {u_m}.
+\]
+If $B_{U,m}$ is the set of vertices with first coordinate nonzero, then
+\begin{equation}
+\ell_{\rm cau}(U,m)=1+sup\{\text{edge length of a path from }B_{U,m}\}.
+\label{eq:pisot-longest-path}
+\end{equation}
+Moreover, $\Phi_{U,m}$ is injective if and only if no directed cycle of
+$\Gamma_{U,m}$ is reachable from $B_{U,m}$.
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:simple-parry-causal-collision} uses only the
+bijection between normal words and the residue interval, together with the
+fact that every $e\in\Delta_U$ is the difference of its positive and
+negative parts in $D_U$.  Those two facts hold here, so the same quotient of
+the classical pair graph gives \eqref{eq:pisot-exact-depth} and
+\eqref{eq:pisot-longest-path}.  A nonzero bi-infinite path is again realized
+by two raw points, and a reachable cycle can be repeated periodically.
+
+It remains only to note why injectivity rules out the zero loop as a
+reachable cycle.  If $d_U\ge u_m$, the constant nonzero difference sequence
+$e_t=u_m$ belongs to $\Delta_U^{\mathbb Z}$ and every window sum is divisible
+by $u_m$; hence $\Phi_{U,m}$ is noninjective and the difference graph has a
+nonzero loop.  In the only remaining case, $d_U<u_m$.  If a vertex has an
+edge to the zero vertex, its overlap coordinates vanish and its first
+coordinate $a$ satisfies $a\equiv0\pmod {u_m}$.  The bound $|a|\le d_U<u_m$
+then gives $a=0$, so the zero vertex is its own unique predecessor.  This
+proves the last assertion without imposing a restriction on the allowed
+nonstandard initial values.
+\end{proof}
+
+We next make the contraction constant explicit.  Let
+$\beta=\beta_0,\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_{s-1}$ be the roots of the minimal
+polynomial, with $\beta>1$ and $|\beta_i|<1$ for $i\ge1$.  The recurrence and
+the initial values effectively give algebraic numbers $c_i$ such that
+\begin{equation}
+u_n=\sum_{i=0}^{s-1}c_i\beta_i^n,
+\qquad c_0>0.
+\label{eq:pisot-binet}
+\end{equation}
+Effective root isolation gives positive algebraic bounds $b_U,A_U$ with
+\begin{equation}
+b_U\beta^n\le u_n\le A_U\beta^n\qquad(n\ge0).
+\label{eq:pisot-effective-growth}
+\end{equation}
+Indeed, isolate a point after which the total conjugate contribution in
+\eqref{eq:pisot-binet} is at most $c_0\beta^n/2$, and inspect the remaining
+finite prefix.
+
+Set
+\begin{equation}
+\widehat K_U=
+\left\lceil\frac{d_UA_U}{b_U(\beta-1)}\right\rceil.
+\label{eq:pisot-analytic-carry-bound}
+\end{equation}
+The bounded-zero normalization automaton may now be intersected with the
+finite terminal alphabet $[-\widehat K_U,\widehat K_U]$.  Let
+$\mathcal K_U$ be the set of terminal carries $k$ for which that automaton
+accepts a word of the form in \eqref{eq:pisot-zero-word-bridge}, and put
+$K_U=\max_{k\in\mathcal K_U}|k|$.  Finite automaton reachability computes
+this set.  Equation \eqref{eq:pisot-effective-growth} shows directly that
+every carry in \eqref{eq:pisot-window-carry} belongs to it, since
+\[
+|k_t|\le d_U\frac{\sum_{j<m}u_j}{u_m}
+<\frac{d_UA_U}{b_U(\beta-1)}.
+\]
+
+For nonintegral $\beta$, define the effective positive separation
+\begin{equation}
+\delta_U=\min\left\{|a+k-\beta l|:
+ a\in\Delta_U,\ k,l\in\mathcal K_U,\ a+k-\beta l\ne0\right\}
+\label{eq:pisot-effective-separation}
+\end{equation}
+and
+\begin{equation}
+M_U=\frac1{c_0}\sum_{i=1}^{s-1}|c_i|
+ \left(\frac{d_U}{1-|\beta_i|}+K_U\right),
+\qquad
+B_U=d_U+(1+\beta)M_U.
+\label{eq:pisot-conjugate-bound}
+\end{equation}
+The minimum in \eqref{eq:pisot-effective-separation} is positive: if
+$l\ne0$, irrationality of $\beta$ prevents equality with the integer
+$a+k$, while for $l=0$ every nonzero value has modulus at least one.  All
+comparisons are comparisons of algebraic numbers and are effective.
+Finally let
+\begin{equation}
+m_U=\min\{m\ge2:\beta^m\delta_U>B_U\}.
+\label{eq:pisot-contraction-threshold}
+\end{equation}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Adjacent-window Pisot contraction]
+\label{lem:pisot-adjacent-window-contraction}
+Suppose that $\beta$ is nonintegral, $m\ge m_U$, and two consecutive rows
+of \eqref{eq:pisot-window-carry} hold.  Then
+\begin{equation}
+k_{t+1}=0,\qquad e_{t+m}=-k_t.
+\label{eq:pisot-carry-collapse}
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+For each embedding define
+\[
+A_{t,i}=\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}e_{t+j}\beta_i^j-k_t\beta_i^m.
+\]
+Substitution of \eqref{eq:pisot-binet} into
+\eqref{eq:pisot-window-carry} gives
+$\sum_i c_iA_{t,i}=0$.  For $i\ge1$,
+\[
+|A_{t,i}|\le \frac{d_U}{1-|\beta_i|}+K_U,
+\]
+and therefore $|A_{t,0}|\le M_U$.  Direct subtraction of two adjacent
+dominant-embedding sums yields
+\begin{equation}
+\beta^m(e_{t+m}+k_t-\beta k_{t+1})
+=\beta A_{t+1,0}-A_{t,0}+e_t.
+\label{eq:pisot-adjacent-binet-identity}
+\end{equation}
+The right side has modulus at most $B_U$.  By
+\eqref{eq:pisot-effective-separation} and
+\eqref{eq:pisot-contraction-threshold}, the parenthesis on the left must
+vanish.  Since $e_{t+m}+k_t$ and $k_{t+1}$ are integers and $\beta$ is
+irrational, this is possible only in \eqref{eq:pisot-carry-collapse}.
+\end{proof}
+
+For $2\le m<m_U$, let $p_U(m)$ be the maximum edge length of a path from
+$B_{U,m}$ when no directed cycle is reachable from $B_{U,m}$, and put
+$p_U(m)=0$ otherwise.  This finite list is computed by exact acyclic
+longest-path searches.  Define
+\begin{equation}
+C_U=\max\left(2,
+ \max_{2\le m<m_U}\left\lceil\frac{1+p_U(m)}m\right\rceil\right).
+\label{eq:effective-linear-constant}
+\end{equation}
+This is a finite, effective recipe from the recurrence, the canonical digit
+set, and the bounded-zero normalization automaton.  The large-aperture part
+of the recipe is the Pisot contraction estimate, not a count of the
+$(2d_U+1)^{m-1}$ difference vertices.
+
+\begin{theorem}[Fixed-base linear causal depth and sharpness for Pisot numeration]
+\label{thm:pisot-linear-depth-sharpness}
+Let $U=(u_j)_{j\ge0}$ be a strictly increasing Pisot numeration system,
+with nonstandard initial values allowed, $u_0=1$, canonical greedy digit set
+$D_U=\{0,\ldots,d_U\}$, and canonical normal words
+\eqref{eq:pisot-canonical-words}.  Assume that $U$ preserves zeros, or,
+equivalently, that its leading Pisot root satisfies Condition~F.  Then the
+constant $C_U<\infty$ in \eqref{eq:effective-linear-constant} is effectively
+computable from the recurrence, the canonical digit set, and the
+bounded-zero normalization automaton, and, for every $m\ge2$,
+\refstepcounter{equation}
+\begin{equation}
+\Phi_{U,m}\text{ injective}
+\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
+\ell_{\rm cau}(U,m)\le C_Um.
+\tag{A1}\label{eq:pisot-linear-A1}
+\end{equation}
+Equivalently, if no first-coordinate-nonzero state of $\Gamma_{U,m}$ can
+reach a directed cycle, every directed path from that initial state set has
+length at most $C_Um-1$.
+
+Let $\theta$ be the real root of
+\[
+x^3-2x^2+x-1
+\]
+and let $U_\theta=(Q_j(\theta))_{j\ge0}$ be given by
+\begin{equation}
+Q_0(\theta)=1,\quad Q_1(\theta)=2,\quad Q_2(\theta)=4,
+\quad Q_{j+3}(\theta)=2Q_{j+2}(\theta)-Q_{j+1}(\theta)+Q_j(\theta).
+\label{eq:theta-count-recurrence}
+\end{equation}
+For every $m\ge4$,
+\refstepcounter{equation}
+\begin{equation}
+\Phi_{\theta,m}\text{ is injective},\qquad
+\ell_{\rm cau}(\theta,m)=2\left\lfloor\frac m2\right\rfloor-1.
+\tag{A2}\label{eq:pisot-linear-A2}
+\end{equation}
+More precisely, if
+$\lambda_m=2\lfloor m/2\rfloor-1$, then
+\refstepcounter{equation}
+\begin{equation}
+\mathcal N_{\theta,m,\lambda_m-1}=\{E_m,-E_m\}\ne\varnothing,
+\qquad
+\mathcal N_{\theta,m,\lambda_m}=\varnothing,
+\tag{A3}\label{eq:pisot-linear-A3}
+\end{equation}
+where, writing concatenation by juxtaposition and changing every sign by a
+prefixed minus,
+\begin{equation}
+\begin{gathered}
+E_4=(1,-1,-1,-1,1),\\
+E_m=(1,0,-E_{m-2},0,0)\quad(m\ge6\text{ even}),\\
+E_m=(E_{m-1},0)\quad(m\ge5\text{ odd}).
+\end{gathered}
+\label{eq:theta-terminal-word}
+\end{equation}
+Consequently
+\[
+\lim_{m\to\infty}\frac{\ell_{\rm cau}(\theta,m)}m=1,
+\]
+so the fixed-system linear upper bound cannot be improved to $o(m)$ in
+growth order.
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+We first prove \eqref{eq:pisot-linear-A1}.  The degree-one case is
+$u_j=b^j$, $D_U=\{0,\ldots,b-1\}$; its fold is the identity and
+$\ell_{\rm cau}(U,m)=1$.  Suppose that $\beta$ is nonintegral and
+$m\ge m_U$.  If a vector in $\mathcal N_{U,m,L}$ has $L\ge2$, apply
+Lemma~\ref{lem:pisot-adjacent-window-contraction} for
+$0\le t\le L-2$.  It gives
+\[
+k_1=\cdots=k_{L-1}=0,\qquad
+e_m=-k_0,\qquad e_{m+1}=\cdots=e_{m+L-2}=0.
+\]
+If $L=m+1$, the terminal difference vertex is therefore zero.  It cannot
+be reached from $B_{U,m}$ when no directed cycle is reachable, because the
+zero vertex has a loop.  Hence every such path has at most $m$ edges and
+$\ell_{\rm cau}(U,m)\le m+1\le2m$.  The finitely many smaller apertures are
+covered by the definition of $C_U$.  Lemma
+\ref{lem:pisot-exact-collision-quotient} gives both formulations of
+\eqref{eq:pisot-linear-A1}.
+
+We turn to $\theta$.  The polynomial is negative at $7/4$, positive at
+$351/200$, and has only one real zero; the product of the two nonreal roots
+has modulus $1/\theta$.  Thus $\theta$ is Pisot.  Its defining equation
+gives
+\[
+1=\theta^{-1}+\theta^{-2}+\theta^{-4},
+\]
+and every proper suffix of $1101\,0^\infty$ is lexicographically smaller.
+Parry's criterion therefore gives $d_\theta(1)=1101\,0^\infty$.  The
+canonical language counts are exactly \eqref{eq:theta-count-recurrence}.
+In particular, the digit and difference alphabets are $\{0,1\}$ and
+$\{-1,0,1\}$.  The recurrence also implies the positive recurrence
+$Q_{n+4}=Q_{n+3}+Q_{n+2}+Q_n$.  Thus
+$2Q_{n+1}-3Q_n>0$ follows from its four positive initial values.  Starting
+with $Q_0<2Q_1$ and using
+$\sum_{j<m+1}Q_j<3Q_m<2Q_{m+1}$ then gives
+\begin{equation}
+\sum_{j<m}Q_j(\theta)<2Q_m(\theta),
+\label{eq:theta-carry-one}
+\end{equation}
+so every window carry belongs to $\{-1,0,1\}$.
+
+For completeness, we verify the contraction threshold rather than invoking
+an unspecified asymptotic.  If $\rho,\overline\rho$ are the nonreal roots,
+write
+\[
+Q_n=c_\theta\theta^n+c_\rho\rho^n+overline{c_\rho}\,\overline\rho^n.
+\]
+The rational isolating interval above and the residue formula for the
+generating function
+\[
+\sum_{n\ge0}Q_nz^n=\frac{1+z^2}{1-2z+z^2-z^3}
+\]
+give
+\[
+1.26<c_\theta<1.27,\qquad |c_\rho|<0.19,\qquad |\rho|<0.756.
+\]
+Hence the dominant-embedding error in the proof of Lemma
+\ref{lem:pisot-adjacent-window-contraction} is less than $1.54$.  Here
+$\delta_\theta=2-\theta>0.245$, and
+\[
+\theta^6\delta_\theta>7.03
+>1+(1+\theta)1.54.
+\]
+It follows that \eqref{eq:pisot-carry-collapse} holds for every $m\ge6$.
+The apertures $m=4,5$ will be included in the exact terminal check below.
+
+It remains to classify the longest paths.  Fix $m\ge6$ and a vector with
+at least two collision rows.  After the carry collapse, all its coordinates
+beyond $m$ vanish except possibly $e_m=-k_0$.  Define the full suffix sums
+\[
+R_t=\sum_{j\ge0}Q_j(\theta)e_{t+j}.
+\]
+Every collision row with $t\ge1$ is now $R_t=0$, and the first row together
+with $e_m=-k_0$ gives $R_0=0$.  The recurrence implies the exact identity
+\begin{equation}
+R_t=e_t+e_{t+2}+2R_{t+1}-R_{t+2}+R_{t+3}.
+\label{eq:theta-suffix-renormalization}
+\end{equation}
+Thus four consecutive zero suffix sums force $e_t=-e_{t+2}$.
+
+Let first $m$ be even and take $L=m-2=\lambda_m-1$.  We have
+$R_t=0$ for $0\le t\le m-3$.  The terminal equation is
+\[
+e_{m-3}+2e_{m-2}+4e_{m-1}+7e_m=0.
+\]
+In $\{-1,0,1\}^4$ its complete solution set is
+\begin{equation}
+(0,0,0,0),\qquad \pm(1,1,1,-1).
+\label{eq:theta-four-tail-table}
+\end{equation}
+The zero tail propagates backwards to the zero word.  From a nonzero tail,
+the equations $R_{m-4}=R_{m-5}=0$ give respectively
+$e_{m-4}=-e_{m-3}$ and $e_{m-5}=0$; then
+\eqref{eq:theta-suffix-renormalization} propagates the alternating pair
+uniquely to the left.  This is precisely the recursion
+\eqref{eq:theta-terminal-word}, and both signs occur.  Hence the first set
+in \eqref{eq:pisot-linear-A3} is $\{\pm E_m\}$.  With one more row, the
+terminal equation is
+\[
+e_{m-2}+2e_{m-1}+4e_m=0,
+\]
+whose only solution in $\{-1,0,1\}^3$ is zero.  Backward propagation then
+contradicts $e_0\ne0$.  Thus $\mathcal N_{\theta,m,\lambda_m}$ is empty.
+
+Now let $m$ be odd and take $L=m-3=\lambda_m-1$.  The terminal five-digit
+equation has, up to sign, exactly the following solutions:
+\begin{equation}
+(0,0,0,0,0),\quad
+(1,1,1,-1,0),\quad
+(1,0,1,1,-1),\quad
+(1,-1,-1,-1,1).
+\label{eq:theta-five-tail-table}
+\end{equation}
+Successive solution of $R_{m-5}=0$ gives respectively
+$0,-1,0,0$ for the preceding digit.  Since $m-5$ is even,
+\eqref{eq:theta-suffix-renormalization} propagates this digit to $e_0$ up
+to sign.  The zero tail and the last two nonzero tails therefore give
+$e_0=0$; only $\pm(1,1,1,-1,0)$ survive.  They give exactly the even
+terminal word for aperture $m-1$ followed by zero, namely $\pm E_m$.
+With one more row the terminal four-digit alternatives are
+\eqref{eq:theta-four-tail-table}; now $m-5$ has even parity and its forced
+zero propagates to $e_0$.  Hence the next obstruction set is empty.
+
+For $m=4,5$, successive exact division in the two or three window
+congruences gives
+\[
+\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
+m&Q_m&\mathcal N_{\theta,m,\lambda_m-1}
+&\mathcal N_{\theta,m,\lambda_m}\\ \hline
+4&12&\{\pm(1,-1,-1,-1,1)\}&\varnothing\\
+5&21&\{\pm(1,-1,-1,-1,1,0)\}&\varnothing.
+\end{array}
+\]
+This is an exhaustive integer calculation: in each row the quotient is in
+$\{-1,0,1\}$ by \eqref{eq:theta-carry-one}, and the last digit determines
+the preceding bounded digit successively.  Thus \eqref{eq:pisot-linear-A3}
+holds for every $m\ge4$.  Lemma
+\ref{lem:pisot-exact-collision-quotient} now gives
+\eqref{eq:pisot-linear-A2}, including injectivity, and the limiting statement
+is immediate.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{corollary}[Bounded-zero strip synchronization]
+\label{cor:pisot-zero-strip-synchronization}
+For a fixed zero-preserving Pisot numeration $U$, consider bounded zero words
+of length $m+1$ of the form
+\[
+[e_t,\ldots,e_{t+m-1},-k_t]_U=0
+\]
+which overlap one digit at a time.  Either
+the resulting strip pumps to a periodic bounded zero representation, or it
+synchronizes in at most $(C_U+1)m$ rows.  This order is $\Theta(m)$ for
+$U_\theta$.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The overlapping rows are exactly paths in $\Gamma_{U,m}$ by
+\eqref{eq:pisot-zero-word-bridge}.  Unless the strip is zero, at most $m-1$
+initial rows pass before a nonzero coordinate occupies the first position.
+A pumpable strip is then a reachable directed cycle; otherwise
+\eqref{eq:pisot-linear-A1} gives the remaining bound.  The words $E_m$ in
+\eqref{eq:pisot-linear-A3} give the matching lower order for $U_\theta$.
+\end{proof}

 \section{Concluding remarks}\label{sec:discussion}
 
+The central conclusion is a fixed-system complexity theorem on a standard
+numeration class.  For every strictly increasing zero-preserving Pisot
+numeration $U$, including systems with nonstandard initial values, Theorem
+\ref{thm:pisot-linear-depth-sharpness} gives an effective constant $C_U$ and
+the uniform implication
+\[
+\Phi_{U,m}\text{ injective}\Longrightarrow
+\ell_{\rm cau}(U,m)\le C_Um.
+\]

+normalization automaton, and finitely many exact small-aperture searches.

+def theta_terminal_vector(m: int) -> tuple[int, ...]:
+    """Return the positive-first extremal word E_m for the fixed cubic base."""
+    if m < 4:
+        raise ValueError("the fixed-theta theorem begins at aperture m=4")
+    even_aperture = m if m % 2 == 0 else m - 1
+    core = (1, -1, -1, -1, 1)
+    for aperture in range(6, even_aperture + 1, 2):
+        core = (1, 0) + tuple(-entry for entry in core)
+        if len(core) != aperture + 1:
+            raise AssertionError("the two-step terminal recursion lost its aperture")
+    vector = core + (0,) * (even_aperture - 4)
+    if m % 2:
+        vector += (0,)
+    return vector

+We study the symbolic dynamics of cyclic recodings of greedy Pisot
+numeration systems.  The canonical rank of a legal length-$m$ word is
+extended to the full digit cube, reduced modulo the number $u_m$ of legal
+words, and overlapped along consecutive windows.  This is a congruence of
+integer language ranks, not numerical $\beta$-normalization in
+$\mathbb Z[\beta]$.
+
+Our first main result is uniform over standard Pisot numeration systems.  If
+a fixed strictly increasing system $U=(u_j)$ preserves zeros, equivalently
+its leading root satisfies Condition~F, there is an effectively computable
+constant $C_U$ such that every injective aperture-$m$ recoding satisfies
 \[
+\ell_{\rm cau}(U,m)\le C_Um.
+\]
+The constant is computed from the recurrence, canonical digit set, and
+bounded-zero normalization automaton.  The proof uses the contracting Pisot
+conjugates to collapse adjacent window carries; it is not a count of the
+exponentially many difference states.  The order is sharp.  For the fixed
+binary cubic system whose leading root $\theta$ satisfies
+$\theta^3-2\theta^2+\theta-1=0$, every $m\ge4$ is injective and
+\[
+\ell_{\rm cau}(\theta,m)=2\lfloor m/2\rfloor-1.
+\]
+We classify the two signed terminal collision words attaining this depth.

 \medskip
+\noindent\textbf{Fixed-base Pisot linear depth.}
+Let $U=(u_j)$ be a strictly increasing Pisot numeration system with
+canonical digit set $D_U=\{0,\ldots,d_U\}$; nonstandard initial values are
+allowed.  Assume that $U$ preserves zeros, equivalently that its leading
+Pisot root satisfies Condition~F
+\cite{FrougnySolomyak1992,CartonSudberyYassawi2026}.  Theorem
+\ref{thm:pisot-linear-depth-sharpness} proves that there is an effectively
+computable $C_U<\infty$ such that
+\[
+\Phi_{U,m}\text{ injective}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
+\ell_{\rm cau}(U,m)\le C_Um\qquad(m\ge2).
+\]
+The constant is obtained from the recurrence, the canonical digit set, and
+the bounded-zero normalization automaton.  Each collision window becomes a
+standard bounded zero representation
+\[
+[e_t,\ldots,e_{t+m-1},-k_t]_U=0.
+\]
+A Binet estimate in the contracting conjugate directions then collapses two
+adjacent carries beyond an effective aperture.  Hence all but one appended
+difference vanish; a path surviving more than linearly many rows would
+reach the zero loop and violate injectivity.  Only finitely many smaller
+apertures require exact graph searches.  Thus the bound uses Pisot
+contraction and normalization data rather than the exponential vertex count
+$(2d_U+1)^{m-1}$.

+\section{Fixed-base linear depth for Pisot numeration}
+\label{sec:pisot-linear-depth}
+
+We now pass from Parry families to a fixed standard numeration system.  A
+Pisot numeration system is a sequence $U=(u_j)_{j\ge0}$ of positive integers
+which satisfies the integral recurrence whose characteristic polynomial is
+the minimal polynomial of a Pisot number; the initial values need not be the
+standard ones.  We assume throughout this section that $U$ is strictly
+increasing and $u_0=1$.  Let
+\[
+D_U=\{0,\ldots,d_U\}
+\]
+be its canonical greedy digit set.  The canonical greedy $U$-normal words of
+length $m$ are
+\begin{equation}
+X_{U,m}=\left\{x\in D_U^m:
+ \sum_{j=0}^k x_ju_j<u_{k+1}\quad(0\le k<m)\right\}.
+\label{eq:pisot-canonical-words}
+\end{equation}
+Thus
+\[
+\Val_{U,m}(x)=\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}x_ju_j
+\]
+maps $X_{U,m}$ bijectively onto $\{0,\ldots,u_m-1\}$.  Define
+\begin{equation}
+\Fold_{U,m}(w)=
+(\Val_{U,m}|_{X_{U,m}})^{-1}
+       (\Val_{U,m}(w)\bmod u_m)
+\label{eq:pisot-canonical-fold}
+\end{equation}
+and let $\Phi_{U,m}$ be the corresponding sliding code on
+$D_U^{\mathbb Z}$.  We use the convention in
+\eqref{eq:simple-parry-causal-length} for $\ell_{\rm cau}(U,m)$.
+
+Put $\Delta_U=[-d_U,d_U]\cap\mathbb Z$ and, for $L\ge1$, set
+\begin{equation}
+\mathcal N_{U,m,L}=\left\{e\in\Delta_U^{m+L-1}:
+ e_0\ne0,\quad
+ \sum_{j=0}^{m-1}u_je_{t+j}\equiv0\pmod {u_m}
+ \ (0\le t<L)\right\}.
+\label{eq:pisot-bad-sliding-set}
+\end{equation}
+Every row in this system has a uniquely defined carry $k_t\in\mathbb Z$:
+\begin{equation}
+\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}u_je_{t+j}=k_tu_m.
+\label{eq:pisot-window-carry}
+\end{equation}
+Equivalently,
+\begin{equation}
+[e_t,e_{t+1},\ldots,e_{t+m-1},-k_t]_U=0,
+\label{eq:pisot-zero-word-bridge}
+\end{equation}
+where the last coordinate has weight $u_m$.  This is the promised bridge to
+the standard language of bounded zero representations; it is not an
+identification with numerical $\beta$-normalization.
+
+\begin{lemma}[Exact collision quotient for $U$]
+\label{lem:pisot-exact-collision-quotient}
+For every $m\ge2$,
+\begin{equation}
+\ell_{\rm cau}(U,m)
+=\min\{L\ge1:\mathcal N_{U,m,L}=\varnothing\}.
+\label{eq:pisot-exact-depth}
+\end{equation}
+Let $\Gamma_{U,m}$ have vertex set $\Delta_U^{m-1}$ and an edge
+$(v_0,\ldots,v_{m-2})\to(v_1,\ldots,v_{m-2},a)$ exactly when
+\[
+\sum_{j=0}^{m-2}u_jv_j+u_{m-1}a\equiv0\pmod {u_m}.
+\]
+If $B_{U,m}$ is the set of vertices with first coordinate nonzero, then
+\begin{equation}
+\ell_{\rm cau}(U,m)=1+sup\{\text{edge length of a path from }B_{U,m}\}.
+\label{eq:pisot-longest-path}
+\end{equation}
+Moreover, $\Phi_{U,m}$ is injective if and only if no directed cycle of
+$\Gamma_{U,m}$ is reachable from $B_{U,m}$.
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:simple-parry-causal-collision} uses only the
+bijection between normal words and the residue interval, together with the
+fact that every $e\in\Delta_U$ is the difference of its positive and
+negative parts in $D_U$.  Those two facts hold here, so the same quotient of
+the classical pair graph gives \eqref{eq:pisot-exact-depth} and
+\eqref{eq:pisot-longest-path}.  A nonzero bi-infinite path is again realized
+by two raw points, and a reachable cycle can be repeated periodically.
+
+It remains only to note why injectivity rules out the zero loop as a
+reachable cycle.  If $d_U\ge u_m$, the constant nonzero difference sequence
+$e_t=u_m$ belongs to $\Delta_U^{\mathbb Z}$ and every window sum is divisible
+by $u_m$; hence $\Phi_{U,m}$ is noninjective and the difference graph has a
+nonzero loop.  In the only remaining case, $d_U<u_m$.  If a vertex has an
+edge to the zero vertex, its overlap coordinates vanish and its first
+coordinate $a$ satisfies $a\equiv0\pmod {u_m}$.  The bound $|a|\le d_U<u_m$
+then gives $a=0$, so the zero vertex is its own unique predecessor.  This
+proves the last assertion without imposing a restriction on the allowed
+nonstandard initial values.
+\end{proof}
+
+We next make the contraction constant explicit.  Let
+$\beta=\beta_0,\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_{s-1}$ be the roots of the minimal
+polynomial, with $\beta>1$ and $|\beta_i|<1$ for $i\ge1$.  The recurrence and
+the initial values effectively give algebraic numbers $c_i$ such that
+\begin{equation}
+u_n=\sum_{i=0}^{s-1}c_i\beta_i^n,
+\qquad c_0>0.
+\label{eq:pisot-binet}
+\end{equation}
+Effective root isolation gives positive algebraic bounds $b_U,A_U$ with
+\begin{equation}
+b_U\beta^n\le u_n\le A_U\beta^n\qquad(n\ge0).
+\label{eq:pisot-effective-growth}
+\end{equation}
+Indeed, isolate a point after which the total conjugate contribution in
+\eqref{eq:pisot-binet} is at most $c_0\beta^n/2$, and inspect the remaining
+finite prefix.
+
+Set
+\begin{equation}
+\widehat K_U=
+\left\lceil\frac{d_UA_U}{b_U(\beta-1)}\right\rceil.
+\label{eq:pisot-analytic-carry-bound}
+\end{equation}
+The bounded-zero normalization automaton may now be intersected with the
+finite terminal alphabet $[-\widehat K_U,\widehat K_U]$.  Let
+$\mathcal K_U$ be the set of terminal carries $k$ for which that automaton
+accepts a word of the form in \eqref{eq:pisot-zero-word-bridge}, and put
+$K_U=\max_{k\in\mathcal K_U}|k|$.  Finite automaton reachability computes
+this set.  Equation \eqref{eq:pisot-effective-growth} shows directly that
+every carry in \eqref{eq:pisot-window-carry} belongs to it, since
+\[
+|k_t|\le d_U\frac{\sum_{j<m}u_j}{u_m}
+<\frac{d_UA_U}{b_U(\beta-1)}.
+\]
+
+For nonintegral $\beta$, define the effective positive separation
+\begin{equation}
+\delta_U=\min\left\{|a+k-\beta l|:
+ a\in\Delta_U,\ k,l\in\mathcal K_U,\ a+k-\beta l\ne0\right\}
+\label{eq:pisot-effective-separation}
+\end{equation}
+and
+\begin{equation}
+M_U=\frac1{c_0}\sum_{i=1}^{s-1}|c_i|
+ \left(\frac{d_U}{1-|\beta_i|}+K_U\right),
+\qquad
+B_U=d_U+(1+\beta)M_U.
+\label{eq:pisot-conjugate-bound}
+\end{equation}
+The minimum in \eqref{eq:pisot-effective-separation} is positive: if
+$l\ne0$, irrationality of $\beta$ prevents equality with the integer
+$a+k$, while for $l=0$ every nonzero value has modulus at least one.  All
+comparisons are comparisons of algebraic numbers and are effective.
+Finally let
+\begin{equation}
+m_U=\min\{m\ge2:\beta^m\delta_U>B_U\}.
+\label{eq:pisot-contraction-threshold}
+\end{equation}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Adjacent-window Pisot contraction]
+\label{lem:pisot-adjacent-window-contraction}
+Suppose that $\beta$ is nonintegral, $m\ge m_U$, and two consecutive rows
+of \eqref{eq:pisot-window-carry} hold.  Then
+\begin{equation}
+k_{t+1}=0,\qquad e_{t+m}=-k_t.
+\label{eq:pisot-carry-collapse}
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+For each embedding define
+\[
+A_{t,i}=\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}e_{t+j}\beta_i^j-k_t\beta_i^m.
+\]
+Substitution of \eqref{eq:pisot-binet} into
+\eqref{eq:pisot-window-carry} gives
+$\sum_i c_iA_{t,i}=0$.  For $i\ge1$,
+\[
+|A_{t,i}|\le \frac{d_U}{1-|\beta_i|}+K_U,
+\]
+and therefore $|A_{t,0}|\le M_U$.  Direct subtraction of two adjacent
+dominant-embedding sums yields
+\begin{equation}
+\beta^m(e_{t+m}+k_t-\beta k_{t+1})
+=\beta A_{t+1,0}-A_{t,0}+e_t.
+\label{eq:pisot-adjacent-binet-identity}
+\end{equation}
+The right side has modulus at most $B_U$.  By
+\eqref{eq:pisot-effective-separation} and
+\eqref{eq:pisot-contraction-threshold}, the parenthesis on the left must
+vanish.  Since $e_{t+m}+k_t$ and $k_{t+1}$ are integers and $\beta$ is
+irrational, this is possible only in \eqref{eq:pisot-carry-collapse}.
+\end{proof}
+
+For $2\le m<m_U$, let $p_U(m)$ be the maximum edge length of a path from
+$B_{U,m}$ when no directed cycle is reachable from $B_{U,m}$, and put
+$p_U(m)=0$ otherwise.  This finite list is computed by exact acyclic
+longest-path searches.  Define
+\begin{equation}
+C_U=\max\left(2,
+ \max_{2\le m<m_U}\left\lceil\frac{1+p_U(m)}m\right\rceil\right).
+\label{eq:effective-linear-constant}
+\end{equation}
+This is a finite, effective recipe from the recurrence, the canonical digit
+set, and the bounded-zero normalization automaton.  The large-aperture part
+of the recipe is the Pisot contraction estimate, not a count of the
+$(2d_U+1)^{m-1}$ difference vertices.
+
+\begin{theorem}[Fixed-base linear causal depth and sharpness for Pisot numeration]
+\label{thm:pisot-linear-depth-sharpness}
+Let $U=(u_j)_{j\ge0}$ be a strictly increasing Pisot numeration system,
+with nonstandard initial values allowed, $u_0=1$, canonical greedy digit set
+$D_U=\{0,\ldots,d_U\}$, and canonical normal words
+\eqref{eq:pisot-canonical-words}.  Assume that $U$ preserves zeros, or,
+equivalently, that its leading Pisot root satisfies Condition~F.  Then the
+constant $C_U<\infty$ in \eqref{eq:effective-linear-constant} is effectively
+computable from the recurrence, the canonical digit set, and the
+bounded-zero normalization automaton, and, for every $m\ge2$,
+\refstepcounter{equation}
+\begin{equation}
+\Phi_{U,m}\text{ injective}
+\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
+\ell_{\rm cau}(U,m)\le C_Um.
+\tag{A1}\label{eq:pisot-linear-A1}
+\end{equation}
+Equivalently, if no first-coordinate-nonzero state of $\Gamma_{U,m}$ can
+reach a directed cycle, every directed path from that initial state set has
+length at most $C_Um-1$.
+
+Let $\theta$ be the real root of
+\[
+x^3-2x^2+x-1
+\]
+and let $U_\theta=(Q_j(\theta))_{j\ge0}$ be given by
+\begin{equation}
+Q_0(\theta)=1,\quad Q_1(\theta)=2,\quad Q_2(\theta)=4,
+\quad Q_{j+3}(\theta)=2Q_{j+2}(\theta)-Q_{j+1}(\theta)+Q_j(\theta).
+\label{eq:theta-count-recurrence}
+\end{equation}
+For every $m\ge4$,
+\refstepcounter{equation}
+\begin{equation}
+\Phi_{\theta,m}\text{ is injective},\qquad
+\ell_{\rm cau}(\theta,m)=2\left\lfloor\frac m2\right\rfloor-1.
+\tag{A2}\label{eq:pisot-linear-A2}
+\end{equation}
+More precisely, if
+$\lambda_m=2\lfloor m/2\rfloor-1$, then
+\refstepcounter{equation}
+\begin{equation}
+\mathcal N_{\theta,m,\lambda_m-1}=\{E_m,-E_m\}\ne\varnothing,
+\qquad
+\mathcal N_{\theta,m,\lambda_m}=\varnothing,
+\tag{A3}\label{eq:pisot-linear-A3}
+\end{equation}
+where, writing concatenation by juxtaposition and changing every sign by a
+prefixed minus,
+\begin{equation}
+\begin{gathered}
+E_4=(1,-1,-1,-1,1),\\
+E_m=(1,0,-E_{m-2},0,0)\quad(m\ge6\text{ even}),\\
+E_m=(E_{m-1},0)\quad(m\ge5\text{ odd}).
+\end{gathered}
+\label{eq:theta-terminal-word}
+\end{equation}
+Consequently
+\[
+\lim_{m\to\infty}\frac{\ell_{\rm cau}(\theta,m)}m=1,
+\]
+so the fixed-system linear upper bound cannot be improved to $o(m)$ in
+growth order.
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+We first prove \eqref{eq:pisot-linear-A1}.  The degree-one case is
+$u_j=b^j$, $D_U=\{0,\ldots,b-1\}$; its fold is the identity and
+$\ell_{\rm cau}(U,m)=1$.  Suppose that $\beta$ is nonintegral and
+$m\ge m_U$.  If a vector in $\mathcal N_{U,m,L}$ has $L\ge2$, apply
+Lemma~\ref{lem:pisot-adjacent-window-contraction} for
+$0\le t\le L-2$.  It gives
+\[
+k_1=\cdots=k_{L-1}=0,\qquad
+e_m=-k_0,\qquad e_{m+1}=\cdots=e_{m+L-2}=0.
+\]
+If $L=m+1$, the terminal difference vertex is therefore zero.  It cannot
+be reached from $B_{U,m}$ when no directed cycle is reachable, because the
+zero vertex has a loop.  Hence every such path has at most $m$ edges and
+$\ell_{\rm cau}(U,m)\le m+1\le2m$.  The finitely many smaller apertures are
+covered by the definition of $C_U$.  Lemma
+\ref{lem:pisot-exact-collision-quotient} gives both formulations of
+\eqref{eq:pisot-linear-A1}.
+
+We turn to $\theta$.  The polynomial is negative at $7/4$, positive at
+$351/200$, and has only one real zero; the product of the two nonreal roots
+has modulus $1/\theta$.  Thus $\theta$ is Pisot.  Its defining equation
+gives
+\[
+1=\theta^{-1}+\theta^{-2}+\theta^{-4},
+\]
+and every proper suffix of $1101\,0^\infty$ is lexicographically smaller.
+Parry's criterion therefore gives $d_\theta(1)=1101\,0^\infty$.  The
+canonical language counts are exactly \eqref{eq:theta-count-recurrence}.
+In particular, the digit and difference alphabets are $\{0,1\}$ and
+$\{-1,0,1\}$.  The recurrence also implies the positive recurrence
+$Q_{n+4}=Q_{n+3}+Q_{n+2}+Q_n$.  Thus
+$2Q_{n+1}-3Q_n>0$ follows from its four positive initial values.  Starting
+with $Q_0<2Q_1$ and using
+$\sum_{j<m+1}Q_j<3Q_m<2Q_{m+1}$ then gives
+\begin{equation}
+\sum_{j<m}Q_j(\theta)<2Q_m(\theta),
+\label{eq:theta-carry-one}
+\end{equation}
+so every window carry belongs to $\{-1,0,1\}$.
+
+For completeness, we verify the contraction threshold rather than invoking
+an unspecified asymptotic.  If $\rho,\overline\rho$ are the nonreal roots,
+write
+\[
+Q_n=c_\theta\theta^n+c_\rho\rho^n+overline{c_\rho}\,\overline\rho^n.
+\]
+The rational isolating interval above and the residue formula for the
+generating function
+\[
+\sum_{n\ge0}Q_nz^n=\frac{1+z^2}{1-2z+z^2-z^3}
+\]
+give
+\[
+1.26<c_\theta<1.27,\qquad |c_\rho|<0.19,\qquad |\rho|<0.756.
+\]
+Hence the dominant-embedding error in the proof of Lemma
+\ref{lem:pisot-adjacent-window-contraction} is less than $1.54$.  Here
+$\delta_\theta=2-\theta>0.245$, and
+\[
+\theta^6\delta_\theta>7.03
+>1+(1+\theta)1.54.
+\]
+It follows that \eqref{eq:pisot-carry-collapse} holds for every $m\ge6$.
+The apertures $m=4,5$ will be included in the exact terminal check below.
+
+It remains to classify the longest paths.  Fix $m\ge6$ and a vector with
+at least two collision rows.  After the carry collapse, all its coordinates
+beyond $m$ vanish except possibly $e_m=-k_0$.  Define the full suffix sums
+\[
+R_t=\sum_{j\ge0}Q_j(\theta)e_{t+j}.
+\]
+Every collision row with $t\ge1$ is now $R_t=0$, and the first row together
+with $e_m=-k_0$ gives $R_0=0$.  The recurrence implies the exact identity
+\begin{equation}
+R_t=e_t+e_{t+2}+2R_{t+1}-R_{t+2}+R_{t+3}.
+\label{eq:theta-suffix-renormalization}
+\end{equation}
+Thus four consecutive zero suffix sums force $e_t=-e_{t+2}$.
+
+Let first $m$ be even and take $L=m-2=\lambda_m-1$.  We have
+$R_t=0$ for $0\le t\le m-3$.  The terminal equation is
+\[
+e_{m-3}+2e_{m-2}+4e_{m-1}+7e_m=0.
+\]
+In $\{-1,0,1\}^4$ its complete solution set is
+\begin{equation}
+(0,0,0,0),\qquad \pm(1,1,1,-1).
+\label{eq:theta-four-tail-table}
+\end{equation}
+The zero tail propagates backwards to the zero word.  From a nonzero tail,
+the equations $R_{m-4}=R_{m-5}=0$ give respectively
+$e_{m-4}=-e_{m-3}$ and $e_{m-5}=0$; then
+\eqref{eq:theta-suffix-renormalization} propagates the alternating pair
+uniquely to the left.  This is precisely the recursion
+\eqref{eq:theta-terminal-word}, and both signs occur.  Hence the first set
+in \eqref{eq:pisot-linear-A3} is $\{\pm E_m\}$.  With one more row, the
+terminal equation is
+\[
+e_{m-2}+2e_{m-1}+4e_m=0,
+\]
+whose only solution in $\{-1,0,1\}^3$ is zero.  Backward propagation then
+contradicts $e_0\ne0$.  Thus $\mathcal N_{\theta,m,\lambda_m}$ is empty.
+
+Now let $m$ be odd and take $L=m-3=\lambda_m-1$.  The terminal five-digit
+equation has, up to sign, exactly the following solutions:
+\begin{equation}
+(0,0,0,0,0),\quad
+(1,1,1,-1,0),\quad
+(1,0,1,1,-1),\quad
+(1,-1,-1,-1,1).
+\label{eq:theta-five-tail-table}
+\end{equation}
+Successive solution of $R_{m-5}=0$ gives respectively
+$0,-1,0,0$ for the preceding digit.  Since $m-5$ is even,
+\eqref{eq:theta-suffix-renormalization} propagates this digit to $e_0$ up
+to sign.  The zero tail and the last two nonzero tails therefore give
+$e_0=0$; only $\pm(1,1,1,-1,0)$ survive.  They give exactly the even
+terminal word for aperture $m-1$ followed by zero, namely $\pm E_m$.
+With one more row the terminal four-digit alternatives are
+\eqref{eq:theta-four-tail-table}; now $m-5$ has even parity and its forced
+zero propagates to $e_0$.  Hence the next obstruction set is empty.
+
+For $m=4,5$, successive exact division in the two or three window
+congruences gives
+\[
+\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
+m&Q_m&\mathcal N_{\theta,m,\lambda_m-1}
+&\mathcal N_{\theta,m,\lambda_m}\\ \hline
+4&12&\{\pm(1,-1,-1,-1,1)\}&\varnothing\\
+5&21&\{\pm(1,-1,-1,-1,1,0)\}&\varnothing.
+\end{array}
+\]
+This is an exhaustive integer calculation: in each row the quotient is in
+$\{-1,0,1\}$ by \eqref{eq:theta-carry-one}, and the last digit determines
+the preceding bounded digit successively.  Thus \eqref{eq:pisot-linear-A3}
+holds for every $m\ge4$.  Lemma
+\ref{lem:pisot-exact-collision-quotient} now gives
+\eqref{eq:pisot-linear-A2}, including injectivity, and the limiting statement
+is immediate.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{corollary}[Bounded-zero strip synchronization]
+\label{cor:pisot-zero-strip-synchronization}
+For a fixed zero-preserving Pisot numeration $U$, consider bounded zero words
+of length $m+1$ of the form
+\[
+[e_t,\ldots,e_{t+m-1},-k_t]_U=0
+\]
+which overlap one digit at a time.  Either
+the resulting strip pumps to a periodic bounded zero representation, or it
+synchronizes in at most $(C_U+1)m$ rows.  This order is $\Theta(m)$ for
+$U_\theta$.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The overlapping rows are exactly paths in $\Gamma_{U,m}$ by
+\eqref{eq:pisot-zero-word-bridge}.  Unless the strip is zero, at most $m-1$
+initial rows pass before a nonzero coordinate occupies the first position.
+A pumpable strip is then a reachable directed cycle; otherwise
+\eqref{eq:pisot-linear-A1} gives the remaining bound.  The words $E_m$ in
+\eqref{eq:pisot-linear-A3} give the matching lower order for $U_\theta$.
+\end{proof}

 \section{Concluding remarks}\label{sec:discussion}
 
+The central conclusion is a fixed-system complexity theorem on a standard
+numeration class.  For every strictly increasing zero-preserving Pisot
+numeration $U$, including systems with nonstandard initial values, Theorem
+\ref{thm:pisot-linear-depth-sharpness} gives an effective constant $C_U$ and
+the uniform implication
+\[
+\Phi_{U,m}\text{ injective}\Longrightarrow

+normalization automaton, and finitely many exact small-aperture searches.

+carries collapse before any exponential difference-state count is used.
+Corollary~\ref{cor:pisot-zero-strip-synchronization} states the same result

   1: \section{Fixed-base linear depth for Pisot numeration}
   2: \label{sec:pisot-linear-depth}
   3: 
   4: We now pass from Parry families to a fixed standard numeration system.  A
   5: Pisot numeration system is a sequence $U=(u_j)_{j\ge0}$ of positive integers
   6: which satisfies the integral recurrence whose characteristic polynomial is
   7: the minimal polynomial of a Pisot number; the initial values need not be the
   8: standard ones.  We assume throughout this section that $U$ is strictly
   9: increasing and $u_0=1$.  Let
  10: \[
  11: D_U=\{0,\ldots,d_U\}
  12: \]
  13: be its canonical greedy digit set.  The canonical greedy $U$-normal words of
  14: length $m$ are
  15: \begin{equation}
  16: X_{U,m}=\left\{x\in D_U^m:
  17:  \sum_{j=0}^k x_ju_j<u_{k+1}\quad(0\le k<m)\right\}.
  18: \label{eq:pisot-canonical-words}
  19: \end{equation}
  20: Thus
  21: \[
  22: \Val_{U,m}(x)=\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}x_ju_j
  23: \]
  24: maps $X_{U,m}$ bijectively onto $\{0,\ldots,u_m-1\}$.  Define
  25: \begin{equation}
  26: \Fold_{U,m}(w)=
  27: (\Val_{U,m}|_{X_{U,m}})^{-1}
  28:        (\Val_{U,m}(w)\bmod u_m)
  29: \label{eq:pisot-canonical-fold}
  30: \end{equation}
  31: and let $\Phi_{U,m}$ be the corresponding sliding code on
  32: $D_U^{\mathbb Z}$.  We use the convention in
  33: \eqref{eq:simple-parry-causal-length} for $\ell_{\rm cau}(U,m)$.
  34: 
  35: Put $\Delta_U=[-d_U,d_U]\cap\mathbb Z$ and, for $L\ge1$, set
  36: \begin{equation}
  37: \mathcal N_{U,m,L}=\left\{e\in\Delta_U^{m+L-1}:
  38:  e_0\ne0,\quad
  39:  \sum_{j=0}^{m-1}u_je_{t+j}\equiv0\pmod {u_m}
  40:  \ (0\le t<L)\right\}.
  41: \label{eq:pisot-bad-sliding-set}
  42: \end{equation}
  43: Every row in this system has a uniquely defined carry $k_t\in\mathbb Z$:
  44: \begin{equation}
  45: \sum_{j=0}^{m-1}u_je_{t+j}=k_tu_m.
  46: \label{eq:pisot-window-carry}
  47: \end{equation}
  48: Equivalently,
  49: \begin{equation}
  50: [e_t,e_{t+1},\ldots,e_{t+m-1},-k_t]_U=0,
  51: \label{eq:pisot-zero-word-bridge}
  52: \end{equation}
  53: where the last coordinate has weight $u_m$.  This is the promised bridge to
  54: the standard language of bounded zero representations; it is not an
  55: identification with numerical $\beta$-normalization.
  56: 
  57: \begin{lemma}[Exact collision quotient for $U$]
  58: \label{lem:pisot-exact-collision-quotient}
  59: For every $m\ge2$,
  60: \begin{equation}
  61: \ell_{\rm cau}(U,m)
  62: =\min\{L\ge1:\mathcal N_{U,m,L}=\varnothing\}.
  63: \label{eq:pisot-exact-depth}
  64: \end{equation}
  65: Let $\Gamma_{U,m}$ have vertex set $\Delta_U^{m-1}$ and an edge
  66: $(v_0,\ldots,v_{m-2})\to(v_1,\ldots,v_{m-2},a)$ exactly when
  67: \[
  68: \sum_{j=0}^{m-2}u_jv_j+u_{m-1}a\equiv0\pmod {u_m}.
  69: \]
  70: If $B_{U,m}$ is the set of vertices with first coordinate nonzero, then
  71: \begin{equation}
  72: \ell_{\rm cau}(U,m)=1+sup\{\text{edge length of a path from }B_{U,m}\}.
  73: \label{eq:pisot-longest-path}
  74: \end{equation}
  75: Moreover, $\Phi_{U,m}$ is injective if and only if no directed cycle of
  76: $\Gamma_{U,m}$ is reachable from $B_{U,m}$.
  77: \end{lemma}
  78: 
  79: \begin{proof}
  80: The proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:simple-parry-causal-collision} uses only the
  81: bijection between normal words and the residue interval, together with the
  82: fact that every $e\in\Delta_U$ is the difference of its positive and
  83: negative parts in $D_U$.  Those two facts hold here, so the same quotient of
  84: the classical pair graph gives \eqref{eq:pisot-exact-depth} and
  85: \eqref{eq:pisot-longest-path}.  A nonzero bi-infinite path is again realized
  86: by two raw points, and a reachable cycle can be repeated periodically.
  87: 
  88: It remains only to note why injectivity rules out the zero loop as a
  89: reachable cycle.  If $d_U\ge u_m$, the constant nonzero difference sequence
  90: $e_t=u_m$ belongs to $\Delta_U^{\mathbb Z}$ and every window sum is divisible
  91: by $u_m$; hence $\Phi_{U,m}$ is noninjective and the difference graph has a
  92: nonzero loop.  In the only remaining case, $d_U<u_m$.  If a vertex has an
  93: edge to the zero vertex, its overlap coordinates vanish and its first
  94: coordinate $a$ satisfies $a\equiv0\pmod {u_m}$.  The bound $|a|\le d_U<u_m$
  95: then gives $a=0$, so the zero vertex is its own unique predecessor.  This
  96: proves the last assertion without imposing a restriction on the allowed
  97: nonstandard initial values.
  98: \end{proof}
  99: 
 100: We next make the contraction constant explicit.  Let
 101: $\beta=\beta_0,\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_{s-1}$ be the roots of the minimal
 102: polynomial, with $\beta>1$ and $|\beta_i|<1$ for $i\ge1$.  The recurrence and
 103: the initial values effectively give algebraic numbers $c_i$ such that
 104: \begin{equation}
 105: u_n=\sum_{i=0}^{s-1}c_i\beta_i^n,
 106: \qquad c_0>0.
 107: \label{eq:pisot-binet}
 108: \end{equation}
 109: Effective root isolation gives positive algebraic bounds $b_U,A_U$ with
 110: \begin{equation}
 111: b_U\beta^n\le u_n\le A_U\beta^n\qquad(n\ge0).
 112: \label{eq:pisot-effective-growth}
 113: \end{equation}
 114: Indeed, isolate a point after which the total conjugate contribution in
 115: \eqref{eq:pisot-binet} is at most $c_0\beta^n/2$, and inspect the remaining
 116: finite prefix.
 117: 
 118: Set
 119: \begin{equation}
 120: \widehat K_U=
 121: \left\lceil\frac{d_UA_U}{b_U(\beta-1)}\right\rceil.
 122: \label{eq:pisot-analytic-carry-bound}
 123: \end{equation}
 124: The bounded-zero normalization automaton may now be intersected with the
 125: finite terminal alphabet $[-\widehat K_U,\widehat K_U]$.  Let
 126: $\mathcal K_U$ be the set of terminal carries $k$ for which that automaton
 127: accepts a word of the form in \eqref{eq:pisot-zero-word-bridge}, and put
 128: $K_U=\max_{k\in\mathcal K_U}|k|$.  Finite automaton reachability computes
 129: this set.  Equation \eqref{eq:pisot-effective-growth} shows directly that
 130: every carry in \eqref{eq:pisot-window-carry} belongs to it, since
 131: \[
 132: |k_t|\le d_U\frac{\sum_{j<m}u_j}{u_m}
 133: <\frac{d_UA_U}{b_U(\beta-1)}.
 134: \]
 135: 
 136: For nonintegral $\beta$, define the effective positive separation
 137: \begin{equation}
 138: \delta_U=\min\left\{|a+k-\beta l|:
 139:  a\in\Delta_U,\ k,l\in\mathcal K_U,\ a+k-\beta l\ne0\right\}
 140: \label{eq:pisot-effective-separation}
 141: \end{equation}
 142: and
 143: \begin{equation}
 144: M_U=\frac1{c_0}\sum_{i=1}^{s-1}|c_i|
 145:  \left(\frac{d_U}{1-|\beta_i|}+K_U\right),
 146: \qquad
 147: B_U=d_U+(1+\beta)M_U.
 148: \label{eq:pisot-conjugate-bound}
 149: \end{equation}
 150: The minimum in \eqref{eq:pisot-effective-separation} is positive: if
 151: $l\ne0$, irrationality of $\beta$ prevents equality with the integer
 152: $a+k$, while for $l=0$ every nonzero value has modulus at least one.  All
 153: comparisons are comparisons of algebraic numbers and are effective.
 154: Finally let
 155: \begin{equation}
 156: m_U=\min\{m\ge2:\beta^m\delta_U>B_U\}.
 157: \label{eq:pisot-contraction-threshold}
 158: \end{equation}
 159: 
 160: \begin{lemma}[Adjacent-window Pisot contraction]
 161: \label{lem:pisot-adjacent-window-contraction}
 162: Suppose that $\beta$ is nonintegral, $m\ge m_U$, and two consecutive rows
 163: of \eqref{eq:pisot-window-carry} hold.  Then
 164: \begin{equation}
 165: k_{t+1}=0,\qquad e_{t+m}=-k_t.
 166: \label{eq:pisot-carry-collapse}
 167: \end{equation}
 168: \end{lemma}
 169: 
 170: \begin{proof}
 171: For each embedding define
 172: \[
 173: A_{t,i}=\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}e_{t+j}\beta_i^j-k_t\beta_i^m.
 174: \]
 175: Substitution of \eqref{eq:pisot-binet} into
 176: \eqref{eq:pisot-window-carry} gives
 177: $\sum_i c_iA_{t,i}=0$.  For $i\ge1$,
 178: \[
 179: |A_{t,i}|\le \frac{d_U}{1-|\beta_i|}+K_U,
 180: \]
 181: and therefore $|A_{t,0}|\le M_U$.  Direct subtraction of two adjacent
 182: dominant-embedding sums yields
 183: \begin{equation}
 184: \beta^m(e_{t+m}+k_t-\beta k_{t+1})
 185: =\beta A_{t+1,0}-A_{t,0}+e_t.
 186: \label{eq:pisot-adjacent-binet-identity}
 187: \end{equation}
 188: The right side has modulus at most $B_U$.  By
 189: \eqref{eq:pisot-effective-separation} and
 190: \eqref{eq:pisot-contraction-threshold}, the parenthesis on the left must
 191: vanish.  Since $e_{t+m}+k_t$ and $k_{t+1}$ are integers and $\beta$ is
 192: irrational, this is possible only in \eqref{eq:pisot-carry-collapse}.
 193: \end{proof}
 194: 
 195: For $2\le m<m_U$, let $p_U(m)$ be the maximum edge length of a path from
 196: $B_{U,m}$ when no directed cycle is reachable from $B_{U,m}$, and put
 197: $p_U(m)=0$ otherwise.  This finite list is computed by exact acyclic
 198: longest-path searches.  Define
 199: \begin{equation}
 200: C_U=\max\left(2,
 201:  \max_{2\le m<m_U}\left\lceil\frac{1+p_U(m)}m\right\rceil\right).
 202: \label{eq:effective-linear-constant}
 203: \end{equation}
 204: This is a finite, effective recipe from the recurrence, the canonical digit
 205: set, and the bounded-zero normalization automaton.  The large-aperture part
 206: of the recipe is the Pisot contraction estimate, not a count of the
 207: $(2d_U+1)^{m-1}$ difference vertices.
 208: 
 209: \begin{theorem}[Fixed-base linear causal depth and sharpness for Pisot numeration]
 210: \label{thm:pisot-linear-depth-sharpness}
 211: Let $U=(u_j)_{j\ge0}$ be a strictly increasing Pisot numeration system,
 212: with nonstandard initial values allowed, $u_0=1$, canonical greedy digit set
 213: $D_U=\{0,\ldots,d_U\}$, and canonical normal words
 214: \eqref{eq:pisot-canonical-words}.  Assume that $U$ preserves zeros, or,
 215: equivalently, that its leading Pisot root satisfies Condition~F.  Then the
 216: constant $C_U<\infty$ in \eqref{eq:effective-linear-constant} is effectively
 217: computable from the recurrence, the canonical digit set, and the
 218: bounded-zero normalization automaton, and, for every $m\ge2$,
 219: \refstepcounter{equation}
 220: \begin{equation}
 221: \Phi_{U,m}\text{ injective}
 222: \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 223: \ell_{\rm cau}(U,m)\le C_Um.
 224: \tag{A1}\label{eq:pisot-linear-A1}
 225: \end{equation}
 226: Equivalently, if no first-coordinate-nonzero state of $\Gamma_{U,m}$ can
 227: reach a directed cycle, every directed path from that initial state set has
 228: length at most $C_Um-1$.
 229: 
 230: Let $\theta$ be the real root of
 231: \[
 232: x^3-2x^2+x-1
 233: \]
 234: and let $U_\theta=(Q_j(\theta))_{j\ge0}$ be given by
 235: \begin{equation}
 236: Q_0(\theta)=1,\quad Q_1(\theta)=2,\quad Q_2(\theta)=4,
 237: \quad Q_{j+3}(\theta)=2Q_{j+2}(\theta)-Q_{j+1}(\theta)+Q_j(\theta).
 238: \label{eq:theta-count-recurrence}
 239: \end{equation}
 240: For every $m\ge4$,
 241: \refstepcounter{equation}
 242: \begin{equation}
 243: \Phi_{\theta,m}\text{ is injective},\qquad
 244: \ell_{\rm cau}(\theta,m)=2\left\lfloor\frac m2\right\rfloor-1.
 245: \tag{A2}\label{eq:pisot-linear-A2}
 246: \end{equation}
 247: More precisely, if
 248: $\lambda_m=2\lfloor m/2\rfloor-1$, then
 249: \refstepcounter{equation}
 250: \begin{equation}
 251: \mathcal N_{\theta,m,\lambda_m-1}=\{E_m,-E_m\}\ne\varnothing,
 252: \qquad
 253: \mathcal N_{\theta,m,\lambda_m}=\varnothing,
 254: \tag{A3}\label{eq:pisot-linear-A3}
 255: \end{equation}
 256: where, writing concatenation by juxtaposition and changing every sign by a
 257: prefixed minus,
 258: \begin{equation}
 259: \begin{gathered}
 260: E_4=(1,-1,-1,-1,1),\\
 261: E_m=(1,0,-E_{m-2},0,0)\quad(m\ge6\text{ even}),\\
 262: E_m=(E_{m-1},0)\quad(m\ge5\text{ odd}).
 263: \end{gathered}
 264: \label{eq:theta-terminal-word}
 265: \end{equation}
 266: Consequently
 267: \[
 268: \lim_{m\to\infty}\frac{\ell_{\rm cau}(\theta,m)}m=1,
 269: \]
 270: so the fixed-system linear upper bound cannot be improved to $o(m)$ in
 271: growth order.
 272: \end{theorem}
 273: 
 274: \begin{proof}
 275: We first prove \eqref{eq:pisot-linear-A1}.  The degree-one case is
 276: $u_j=b^j$, $D_U=\{0,\ldots,b-1\}$; its fold is the identity and
 277: $\ell_{\rm cau}(U,m)=1$.  Suppose that $\beta$ is nonintegral and
 278: $m\ge m_U$.  If a vector in $\mathcal N_{U,m,L}$ has $L\ge2$, apply
 279: Lemma~\ref{lem:pisot-adjacent-window-contraction} for
 280: $0\le t\le L-2$.  It gives
 281: \[
 282: k_1=\cdots=k_{L-1}=0,\qquad
 283: e_m=-k_0,\qquad e_{m+1}=\cdots=e_{m+L-2}=0.
 284: \]
 285: If $L=m+1$, the terminal difference vertex is therefore zero.  It cannot
 286: be reached from $B_{U,m}$ when no directed cycle is reachable, because the
 287: zero vertex has a loop.  Hence every such path has at most $m$ edges and
 288: $\ell_{\rm cau}(U,m)\le m+1\le2m$.  The finitely many smaller apertures are
 289: covered by the definition of $C_U$.  Lemma
 290: \ref{lem:pisot-exact-collision-quotient} gives both formulations of
 291: \eqref{eq:pisot-linear-A1}.
 292: 
 293: We turn to $\theta$.  The polynomial is negative at $7/4$, positive at
 294: $351/200$, and has only one real zero; the product of the two nonreal roots
 295: has modulus $1/\theta$.  Thus $\theta$ is Pisot.  Its defining equation
 296: gives
 297: \[
 298: 1=\theta^{-1}+\theta^{-2}+\theta^{-4},
 299: \]
 300: and every proper suffix of $1101\,0^\infty$ is lexicographically smaller.
 301: Parry's criterion therefore gives $d_\theta(1)=1101\,0^\infty$.  The
 302: canonical language counts are exactly \eqref{eq:theta-count-recurrence}.
 303: In particular, the digit and difference alphabets are $\{0,1\}$ and
 304: $\{-1,0,1\}$.  The recurrence also implies the positive recurrence
 305: $Q_{n+4}=Q_{n+3}+Q_{n+2}+Q_n$.  Thus
 306: $2Q_{n+1}-3Q_n>0$ follows from its four positive initial values.  Starting
 307: with $Q_0<2Q_1$ and using
 308: $\sum_{j<m+1}Q_j<3Q_m<2Q_{m+1}$ then gives
 309: \begin{equation}
 310: \sum_{j<m}Q_j(\theta)<2Q_m(\theta),
 311: \label{eq:theta-carry-one}
 312: \end{equation}
 313: so every window carry belongs to $\{-1,0,1\}$.
 314: 
 315: For completeness, we verify the contraction threshold rather than invoking
 316: an unspecified asymptotic.  If $\rho,\overline\rho$ are the nonreal roots,
 317: write
 318: \[
 319: Q_n=c_\theta\theta^n+c_\rho\rho^n+overline{c_\rho}\,\overline\rho^n.
 320: \]
 321: The rational isolating interval above and the residue formula for the
 322: generating function
 323: \[
 324: \sum_{n\ge0}Q_nz^n=\frac{1+z^2}{1-2z+z^2-z^3}
 325: \]
 326: give
 327: \[
 328: 1.26<c_\theta<1.27,\qquad |c_\rho|<0.19,\qquad |\rho|<0.756.
 329: \]
 330: Hence the dominant-embedding error in the proof of Lemma
 331: \ref{lem:pisot-adjacent-window-contraction} is less than $1.54$.  Here
 332: $\delta_\theta=2-\theta>0.245$, and
 333: \[
 334: \theta^6\delta_\theta>7.03
 335: >1+(1+\theta)1.54.
 336: \]
 337: It follows that \eqref{eq:pisot-carry-collapse} holds for every $m\ge6$.
 338: The apertures $m=4,5$ will be included in the exact terminal check below.
 339: 
 340: It remains to classify the longest paths.  Fix $m\ge6$ and a vector with
 341: at least two collision rows.  After the carry collapse, all its coordinates
 342: beyond $m$ vanish except possibly $e_m=-k_0$.  Define the full suffix sums
 343: \[
 344: R_t=\sum_{j\ge0}Q_j(\theta)e_{t+j}.
 345: \]
 346: Every collision row with $t\ge1$ is now $R_t=0$, and the first row together
 347: with $e_m=-k_0$ gives $R_0=0$.  The recurrence implies the exact identity
 348: \begin{equation}
 349: R_t=e_t+e_{t+2}+2R_{t+1}-R_{t+2}+R_{t+3}.
 350: \label{eq:theta-suffix-renormalization}
 351: \end{equation}
 352: Thus four consecutive zero suffix sums force $e_t=-e_{t+2}$.
 353: 
 354: Let first $m$ be even and take $L=m-2=\lambda_m-1$.  We have
 355: $R_t=0$ for $0\le t\le m-3$.  The terminal equation is
 356: \[
 357: e_{m-3}+2e_{m-2}+4e_{m-1}+7e_m=0.
 358: \]
 359: In $\{-1,0,1\}^4$ its complete solution set is
 360: \begin{equation}
 361: (0,0,0,0),\qquad \pm(1,1,1,-1).
 362: \label{eq:theta-four-tail-table}
 363: \end{equation}
 364: The zero tail propagates backwards to the zero word.  From a nonzero tail,
 365: the equations $R_{m-4}=R_{m-5}=0$ give respectively
 366: $e_{m-4}=-e_{m-3}$ and $e_{m-5}=0$; then
 367: \eqref{eq:theta-suffix-renormalization} propagates the alternating pair
 368: uniquely to the left.  This is precisely the recursion
 369: \eqref{eq:theta-terminal-word}, and both signs occur.  Hence the first set
 370: in \eqref{eq:pisot-linear-A3} is $\{\pm E_m\}$.  With one more row, the
 371: terminal equation is
 372: \[
 373: e_{m-2}+2e_{m-1}+4e_m=0,
 374: \]
 375: whose only solution in $\{-1,0,1\}^3$ is zero.  Backward propagation then
 376: contradicts $e_0\ne0$.  Thus $\mathcal N_{\theta,m,\lambda_m}$ is empty.
 377: 
 378: Now let $m$ be odd and take $L=m-3=\lambda_m-1$.  The terminal five-digit
 379: equation has, up to sign, exactly the following solutions:
 380: \begin{equation}
 381: (0,0,0,0,0),\quad
 382: (1,1,1,-1,0),\quad
 383: (1,0,1,1,-1),\quad
 384: (1,-1,-1,-1,1).
 385: \label{eq:theta-five-tail-table}
 386: \end{equation}
 387: Successive solution of $R_{m-5}=0$ gives respectively
 388: $0,-1,0,0$ for the preceding digit.  Since $m-5$ is even,
 389: \eqref{eq:theta-suffix-renormalization} propagates this digit to $e_0$ up
 390: to sign.  The zero tail and the last two nonzero tails therefore give
 391: $e_0=0$; only $\pm(1,1,1,-1,0)$ survive.  They give exactly the even
 392: terminal word for aperture $m-1$ followed by zero, namely $\pm E_m$.
 393: With one more row the terminal four-digit alternatives are
 394: \eqref{eq:theta-four-tail-table}; now $m-5$ has even parity and its forced
 395: zero propagates to $e_0$.  Hence the next obstruction set is empty.
 396: 
 397: For $m=4,5$, successive exact division in the two or three window
 398: congruences gives
 399: \[
 400: \begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
 401: m&Q_m&\mathcal N_{\theta,m,\lambda_m-1}
 402: &\mathcal N_{\theta,m,\lambda_m}\\ \hline
 403: 4&12&\{\pm(1,-1,-1,-1,1)\}&\varnothing\\
 404: 5&21&\{\pm(1,-1,-1,-1,1,0)\}&\varnothing.
 405: \end{array}
 406: \]
 407: This is an exhaustive integer calculation: in each row the quotient is in
 408: $\{-1,0,1\}$ by \eqref{eq:theta-carry-one}, and the last digit determines
 409: the preceding bounded digit successively.  Thus \eqref{eq:pisot-linear-A3}
 410: holds for every $m\ge4$.  Lemma
 411: \ref{lem:pisot-exact-collision-quotient} now gives
 412: \eqref{eq:pisot-linear-A2}, including injectivity, and the limiting statement
 413: is immediate.
 414: \end{proof}
 415: 
 416: \begin{corollary}[Bounded-zero strip synchronization]
 417: \label{cor:pisot-zero-strip-synchronization}
 418: For a fixed zero-preserving Pisot numeration $U$, consider bounded zero words
 419: of length $m+1$ of the form
 420: \[
 421: [e_t,\ldots,e_{t+m-1},-k_t]_U=0
 422: \]
 423: which overlap one digit at a time.  Either
 424: the resulting strip pumps to a periodic bounded zero representation, or it
 425: synchronizes in at most $(C_U+1)m$ rows.  This order is $\Theta(m)$ for
 426: $U_\theta$.
 427: \end{corollary}
 428: 
 429: \begin{proof}
 430: The overlapping rows are exactly paths in $\Gamma_{U,m}$ by
 431: \eqref{eq:pisot-zero-word-bridge}.  Unless the strip is zero, at most $m-1$
 432: initial rows pass before a nonzero coordinate occupies the first position.
 433: A pumpable strip is then a reachable directed cycle; otherwise
 434: \eqref{eq:pisot-linear-A1} gives the remaining bound.  The words $E_m$ in
 435: \eqref{eq:pisot-linear-A3} give the matching lower order for $U_\theta$.
 436: \end{proof}
